newsitem.title: USA: Stocks edge lower, Nasdaq barely changed.
newsitem.headline: Stocks edge lower, Nasdaq barely changed.

text.p: Blue-chip stocks edged lower Wednesday after regrouping from an early sell-off, while the Nasdaq market gave up early gains and was off modestly.

Just after 1:20 p.m. EST, the Dow Jones industrial average was down 21.89 points at 7,290.26. The index lost more than 50 points earlier in the session, prompting the New York Stock Exchange to set trading curbs and then pull them 20 minutes later.
In the broader market, declining issues outpaced gainers by 12 to 10 on volume of 267 million on the NYSE.

The Nasdaq market, where high-tech stocks got clobbered on Tuesday after several companies warned about profits, was higher most of the morning. But the Nasdaq composite index was off 2.09 points at 1,382.82 after falling 1.4 percent on Tuesday.
Stocks fell early along with bonds on news that April factory orders rose a surprisingly strong 1.2 percent compared with a decline of 1.3 percent in March.
The Dow came back along with bonds. The benchmark 30-year Treasury fell 2/32, raising its yield to 6.88 percent. Prices and yields move in opposite directions.
Market-watchers said most big stocks would be stuck in a narrow range, probably tied closely to moves in the bond market, ahead of Friday's key May employment report.

"The market is only going to get nervous about interest rates if they go up a lot," said Roy Blumberg, chief investment strategist at Josephthal Lyon & Ross. "But if rates go up a little or stay where they are, the bond market is not really a consideration."
The bond market was seen quietly biding time until the release of the jobs report on Friday. Before then, and maybe afterwards, stocks were seen staying calm.
"We're in a trading range, which we might be in for the rest of the summer," said Bill Allyn, head of trading at Jefferies & Co.

Stocks would shy away from large moves in either direction because of the broader market's high valuation and because of investors' incessant rotation among groups like technology, financials and small-capitalisation shares, Allyn said.
But investors continued to juggle high-tech stocks, creating a mixed and confusing market in that sector by selectively buying and selling shares, analysts said.
On Tuesday, technology stocks sank after warnings of weak earnings from disk drive maker Seagate Technology Inc. and Cabletron Systems Inc., a maker of computer network gear.

On Wednesday, Cabletron added 5/8 to 30-3/4, but other networking stocks were lower. Bay Networks Inc. slid 1/8 to 22-1/4 and Ascend Communications Inc. fell 3-11/16 to 46-5/8. Bellwether Intel Corp. was off 1 at 144 and Microsoft Corp. fell 3/4 to 120.
The American Stock Exchange index fell 0.57 point to 608.45.
The Russell 2000 index of smaller stocks lost 0.39 point to 382.89.
